implementation: Independent 1.31 host moderation; no 1.29 gameplay header or game RVA is enabled. Standard Winsock ABI observers are installed only after existing executable/profile validation and Local authorization. Existing independently verified 1.31 Resource profiles read the local player name when a world exists; registry userlocal is a lobby fallback.

runtime_protocol_profile.framing: F7 + type + uint16 size; bounded fragmented/coalesced TCP streams
host_evidence: received REQJOIN with bounded valid UTF8 name
sent SLOTINFOJOIN on that same socket, exact nine-byte slot schema and matching recipient ID
current human slot list containing that local player ID
revocations: malformed known-peer traffic or unobservable callback I/O
EOF/socket close/reuse; room and socket epochs reject stale completions

persistence: TS-Banned.ini / [Banned List], name -> reason, same schema as 1.29
transport: send, recv, closesocket, WSASend, WSARecv, GetQueuedCompletionStatus/Ex, WSAGetOverlappedResult; actual completed byte counts, no MSG_PEEK duplication, nested-call suppression, original return/error preservation
limits: No fabricated host/bot privileges. Unrecognized/encrypted traffic never grants kick capability.
Callback-routine overlapped I/O revokes affected proof instead of guessing completion.
Only socket shutdown is requested; actual player departure is game-controlled.
No live two-client Warcraft room or Battle.net/host-bot session has been tested.
No native lobby message pane is ported: command outcomes always go to WHT.log and additionally to native game notification when CGameUI is available.
